title: Retro DJ Material Remix Studio
description: A retro DJ booth scene where sunglasses sit atop a boombox. The user remixes material properties across both objects using coupled sliders and a shared energy conservation system. Metalness added to one object must be subtracted from the other, and all changes support full undo/redo history.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads SunglassesKhronos.glb and BoomBox.glb using GLTFLoader. Position the boombox at center and the sunglasses resting on top of it. Use a PerspectiveCamera at distance 1.5 angled slightly down, with OrbitControls. Add an HDR-style environment using PMREMGenerator with a simple procedural equirect or a neutral studio lighting setup with two directional lights and ambient light. Build a left-side HTML panel titled 'Material Remix Studio' with these coupled controls: (1) A 'Metalness Balance' slider (range 0-1) that sets boombox metalness to the slider value and sunglasses metalness to 1 minus that value, enforcing conservation. (2) A 'Roughness Balance' slider working identically for roughness across both models. (3) A shared 'Tint Hue' color wheel (0-360) that applies a hue-shifted emissive color to both objects simultaneously. (4) Individual 'Opacity' sliders for each object (0-1) enabling transparency on their materials. (5) A 'Clearcoat' toggle button that applies clearcoat=1.0 to whichever object currently has higher metalness. (6) An 'Envmap Intensity' slider (0-3) shared across both objects. Track every slider or toggle change as a state snapshot in an undo/redo stack. Add Undo and Redo buttons that restore full material state for both objects. Display a small HUD showing current total metalness sum (should always equal 1.0) and total roughness sum (should always equal 1.0) to visualize the conservation law. Ensure all meshes in each loaded model have their materials converted to MeshPhysicalMaterial if not already. The interaction requires 10-14 steps to fully explore all controls, verify conservation, and test undo/redo. Use requestAnimationFrame for rendering. Style the UI with dark semi-transparent background and white text.
